result.title: Input-Space versus Feature-Level Conditioning for Robust Facial Expression Recognition
result.summary: Facial expression recognition (FER) degrades sharply when illumination, exposure or resolution departs from the training distribution. Two remedies dominate practice: enriching the input signal, or conditioning intermediate features on an estimated image quality. The two are rarely compared under matched backbones, training budgets and condition annotations, and their cost is seldom reported. We present a controlled comparison on RAF-DB. Input-space conditioning uses four deterministic, label-free views (logarithmic stretching, inverse-logarithmic stretching, down-up resampling and identity), each processed by a shared backbone with a branch-specific BatchNorm and linear head, with the branch logits averaged. Feature-space conditioning is implemented as FiLM and Conditional BatchNorm under an identical protocol. Across six backbone architectures the input-space variant improves top-1 accuracy on every one (mean +0.94 percentage points; bootstrap interval [0.51, 1.63]; sign test p = 0.016), with a seed-controlled estimate of +0.42 percentage points on ResNet-18, whereas feature-level conditioning yields +0.10 and +0.03 percentage points. We attribute the gap to the information content of the heuristic condition label rather than to the conditioning mechanism. The gain costs 4.00x FLOPs, 4.18x latency and 3.79x training time, i.e. 0.26 percentage points per additional GFLOP, and we state an explicit rule for when the trade is worth making.

AI.brief_summary: 在 RAF-DB 上以匹配的骨干、训练预算与条件标注，控制对比输入空间多视图条件化与特征级 FiLM／Conditional BatchNorm 条件化在面部表情识别鲁棒性上的收益，并报告 FLOPs、延迟与训练时间代价。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「输入级条件化保留更多信息、特征级条件化增益甚微」的归因与显式成本核算，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据应经输入旁路还是隐状态条件注入，以及表征条件化是否造成信息坍缩；属较远任务的借鉴线索，需自行判断可迁移性。
